values: Graft macOS app, CLI, sidecar review loop, repo-local agent skill

preview: Graft macOS app, CLI, sidecar review loop, repo-local agent skill

values: As a writer, I want to open a folder workspace so Graft can work with my Markdown files on disk.
Open Workspace presents a directory picker and loads the chosen folder as the workspace root.
Sources/Graft/Stores/WorkspaceStore.swift openWorkspacePanel/openWorkspace; verified by source inspection plus successful serial build/run unless a narrower smoke test is named.
As a developer preview user, I want sample vault bootstrap available without forcing a first-launch privacy prompt on every run.
In DEBUG, bootstrap does nothing by default; when GRAFT_OPEN_SAMPLE_ON_LAUNCH=1 is set, it opens SampleVault relative to the built app bundle.
Final launch screenshot showed empty workspace with no Desktop permission prompt.
As a workspace owner, I want Graft to create local sidecar folders and an agent editing contract so external tools know how to cooperate.
Opening a workspace prepares .graft/history and .graft/shares and writes AGENTS.md only if it is missing.
VersionHistoryStore.prepare + AgentInstructionsWriter.writeIfMissing; verified by source inspection plus successful serial build/run unless a narrower smoke test is named.
As a writer, I want the sidebar to list my Markdown files so I can choose what to edit.
The file list recursively includes .md files, excludes hidden files, .graft contents, and AGENTS.md, then sorts by relative path.
WorkspaceStore.reloadFileList; verified by source inspection plus successful serial build/run unless a narrower smoke test is named.
As a writer, I want selecting a file to load its current contents and related history/reviews.
Selecting a Markdown file saves any dirty current file, loads UTF-8 text, clears external-change banners, selects a matching pending review, and refreshes snapshots.
WorkspaceStore.load(file:); verified by source inspection plus successful serial build/run unless a narrower smoke test is named.
As a writer, I want Save to write my Markdown to disk without changing the storage format.
Save snapshots the current content, writes UTF-8 Markdown to the selected file, updates the clean baseline, reloads the file list, and refreshes history.
WorkspaceStore.saveCurrentDocument; verified by source inspection plus successful serial build/run unless a narrower smoke test is named.
As a writer, I want a plain Markdown editor that does not apply rich-text substitutions.
The editor uses NSTextView as plain text, disables smart substitutions/spell correction, keeps undo enabled, tracks selection, and applies syntax highlighting.
MarkdownTextView + MarkdownSyntaxHighlighter; verified by source inspection plus successful serial build/run unless a narrower smoke test is named.
As a writer, I want Edit, Split, and Preview modes so I can choose between writing and reading.
The toolbar/menu segmented control switches between editor-only, preview-only, and split editor/preview layouts.
EditorContainerView + GraftCommands; verified by source inspection plus successful serial build/run unless a narrower smoke test is named.
As a writer, I want the inspector to open without crushing a three-column editor layout.
Opening the inspector while in Split mode moves the editor to Preview mode; requesting Split while inspector is visible keeps Preview active.
WorkspaceStore.toggleInspector/setEditorMode; verified by source inspection plus successful serial build/run unless a narrower smoke test is named.
As a writer, I want the autosave setting to persist each edit automatically when enabled.
When enabled, edits are written to disk through a snapshot-free autosave path without requiring the Save command.
MarkdownEditorView setter calls WorkspaceStore.autosaveCurrentDocumentIfNeeded; serial build passed.
As a reader, I want Markdown preview to render common block types so I can review the document visually.
Preview renders headings, paragraphs, quotes, unordered lists, ordered lists with source numbers, tasks, code fences with language labels, tables, local images, and horizontal rules.
MarkdownRenderer + MarkdownPreviewView; verified by source inspection plus successful serial build/run unless a narrower smoke test is named.
As a reader, I want inline links and code to remain readable in preview.
Inline Markdown uses AttributedString(markdown:) and styles links and inline code with Graft colors.
MarkdownPreviewView.MarkdownInlineText; verified by source inspection plus successful serial build/run unless a narrower smoke test is named.
As a writer, I want to insert a local image into a document with portable relative Markdown.
Insert Image accepts common image types, copies the file into assets/<document path>/ with a sanitized collision-safe name, appends a relative Markdown image tag, and snapshots the insertion.
WorkspaceStore.insertImageFromPanel + ImageImportService; verified by source inspection plus successful serial build/run unless a narrower smoke test is named.
As a reader, I want local Markdown images to render from the selected document's folder.
Preview resolves image paths relative to the selected file directory and shows either the image with alt/path metadata or a missing-image card.
MarkdownPreviewView.imageView; verified by source inspection plus successful serial build/run unless a narrower smoke test is named.
As a writer, I want to disable external-agent detection when I do not want disk edits captured.
When Show external agent changes is off, file watcher events are ignored.
WorkspaceStore.handleExternalChange guard; verified by source inspection plus successful serial build/run unless a narrower smoke test is named.
As a writer, I want external edits to become reviewable proposals before replacing my current file.
A disk change against the clean selected file creates a pending review, restores the clean base text to disk/app state, selects the review, and shows a review banner.
WorkspaceStore.handleExternalChange/createReview; verified by source inspection plus successful serial build/run unless a narrower smoke test is named.
As a writer, I want my unsaved draft protected when an external edit lands on the same file.
If the selected file is dirty, Graft snapshots the conflict base, creates a conflict review, preserves the human draft, and shows a conflict banner.
WorkspaceStore.handleExternalChange/createReview; verified by source inspection plus successful serial build/run unless a narrower smoke test is named.
Detect external edit in another file
As a writer, I want agent edits to other Markdown files queued for review without interrupting my current document.
A disk change to another known Markdown file creates a pending review for that file and restores that file's baseline until reviewed.
WorkspaceStore.handleExternalChange; verified by source inspection plus successful serial build/run unless a narrower smoke test is named.
As a reviewer, I want pending and conflicting agent edits visible in a side rail.
Review rail shows count, summary, author, file path, hunk count, conflict badge, and focuses the related file/review when selected.
ReviewRailView + WorkspaceStore.focus; verified by source inspection plus successful serial build/run unless a narrower smoke test is named.
As a reviewer, I want to compare current and proposed Markdown before deciding.
Selected reviews show summary, author/file metadata, hunk count, current/proposed diff blocks, and conflict comparison columns when relevant.
InlineDiffView + ConflictResolutionView; verified by source inspection plus successful serial build/run unless a narrower smoke test is named.
As a reviewer, I want to accept an agent proposal when it still matches my draft.
Accept all applies every hunk to the current base, snapshots first, writes the accepted text to disk, marks the review accepted, removes it from pending, and refreshes history.
WorkspaceStore.accept(changeSet) + MarkdownPatchEngine; verified by source inspection plus successful serial build/run unless a narrower smoke test is named.
As a reviewer, I want to reject an agent proposal and keep my visible draft.
Reject all marks the review rejected, removes it from pending, and writes the visible draft back to disk for the selected file.
WorkspaceStore.reject(changeSet); verified by source inspection plus successful serial build/run unless a narrower smoke test is named.
As a reviewer, I want to make a per-hunk decision so I can keep only useful agent changes.
Accept/reject hunk updates the document or keeps the draft, removes the decided hunk, writes an accepted/rejected final review when no hunks remain, and keeps remaining hunks pending.
WorkspaceStore.accept/reject(range:from:); verified by source inspection plus successful serial build/run unless a narrower smoke test is named.
As a reviewer, I want stale proposals to be blocked rather than applied incorrectly.
If the current draft no longer matches the review base or hunk before text, Graft converts the review to conflict and shows a conflict banner.
WorkspaceStore.accept + MarkdownPatchEngine.staleHunk; verified by source inspection plus successful serial build/run unless a narrower smoke test is named.
As a writer, I want local checkpoints before risky operations.
Manual checkpoint, save, restore, review accept, image insert, and review packet actions create Markdown snapshots with front matter under .graft/history/<safe file>/.
VersionHistoryStore + WorkspaceStore.snapshotCurrentDocument; verified by source inspection plus successful serial build/run unless a narrower smoke test is named.
As a writer, I want to restore an earlier version of a Markdown file.
Restore loads snapshot content after front matter, snapshots the current content first, writes restored text to disk, updates baseline, and refreshes history.
WorkspaceStore.restore + VersionHistoryStore.restoreContent; verified by source inspection plus successful serial build/run unless a narrower smoke test is named.
As a collaborator, I want a local checkpoint before sharing review context externally.
Create Packet Checkpoint snapshots the current file and shows a banner; pending reviews are listed with Show Review actions.
ShareView + WorkspaceStore.createReviewPacket; verified by source inspection plus successful serial build/run unless a narrower smoke test is named.
Show agent activity and CLI commands
As a writer using agents, I want the inspector to show recent detected activity and the right CLI commands.
Agents tab shows the latest file-watcher activity or an empty state plus Status, Checkpoint, and Apply command examples.
InspectorView AgentsPanel; verified by source inspection plus successful serial build/run unless a narrower smoke test is named.
As a writer, I want to change the editor font size for readability.
The Settings stepper updates editorFontSize in the store and MarkdownTextView refreshes attributes with the new font.
SettingsView + MarkdownTextView.needsAttributeRefresh; verified by source inspection plus successful serial build/run unless a narrower smoke test is named.
As a keyboard user, I want commands for opening, saving, snapshotting, mode changes, and the inspector.
The app adds menu commands for Open Workspace, Save Document, Snapshot Version, Editor Mode picker, and Toggle Inspector with shortcuts.
GraftCommands; verified by source inspection plus successful serial build/run unless a narrower smoke test is named.
As an agent, I want to inspect a Graft vault before editing.
graft-cli status prints vault path, Markdown file count, sidecar path, pending change metadata count, up to 12 files, and up to 6 change metadata filenames.
Sources/GraftCLI/main.swift status; verified by source inspection plus successful serial build/run unless a narrower smoke test is named.
As an agent, I want to register a completed edit summary for Graft review.
graft-cli submit-change writes .graft/changes metadata with agent and summary and creates a snapshot of the edited file.
Sources/GraftCLI/main.swift submitChange; verified by source inspection plus successful serial build/run unless a narrower smoke test is named.
As an agent, I want to checkpoint a file before editing.
graft-cli snapshot writes a front-matter Markdown snapshot under .graft/history/<safe file>/.
Sources/GraftCLI/main.swift snapshot; verified by source inspection plus successful serial build/run unless a narrower smoke test is named.
As an agent, I expect an apply command either to apply a pending change or to make its snapshot-only behavior explicit.
The command is retained only as a legacy snapshot-only alias and main workflow copy uses submit-change.
Legacy apply printed snapshot-only note; README, sample vault, inspector, and skill now use submit-change.
As an agent, I want to inspect local history and submitted changes for a file.
graft-cli history lists snapshots newest first and then submitted change metadata matching the file.
Sources/GraftCLI/main.swift history; verified by source inspection plus successful serial build/run unless a narrower smoke test is named.
As an external coding agent, I want a clear workflow for editing Graft workspaces.
skills/graft-sync/SKILL.md instructs agents to read AGENTS.md, inspect status, snapshot before broad edits, edit Markdown directly, submit metadata, and leave reviews to Graft.
graft-sync skill uses submit-change and no longer presents apply as the main workflow.
As a first-time user, I want the empty workspace screen to be readable and actionable.
With no workspace open, the first screen shows readable Graft branding, a clear Open Workspace CTA, no Desktop permission prompt, and an empty Agent Edits rail.
As a tester, I want the run script to build and launch reliably from Codex.
script/build_and_run.sh builds with serial Swift jobs by default, stages dist/Graft.app, launches it, and --verify confirms the Graft process exists.
As a maintainer, I want hidden collaboration APIs tracked separately so they are not mistaken for shipped user-facing UX.
WorkspaceStore can add/remove/compose invite metadata, but no current view exposes these methods.
WorkspaceStore invite methods; ShareView has no invite form

values: The Settings UI exposed autosave, but no editor change path observed autosaveEnabled when editorText changed.
Fixed by routing MarkdownEditorView text changes through WorkspaceStore.autosaveCurrentDocumentIfNeeded; build passed.
graft-cli apply only writes a snapshot; it does not apply a pending change or review. README/SampleVault language presented it as an apply workflow.
Fixed copy and CLI note; smoke test confirmed apply prints snapshot-only alias note and workflow examples use submit-change.
CLI relative paths and rapid snapshots were wrong
CLI status printed /privatedocs paths for /tmp vaults, and second-level snapshot IDs overwrote rapid snapshots.
Fixed URL standardization and millisecond snapshot IDs; smoke test produced docs/one.md and three distinct history files.
Default launch triggered Desktop privacy prompt
DEBUG bootstrap opened a Desktop sample vault automatically, causing a macOS permission prompt before the first screen.
Fixed bootstrap to be opt-in via GRAFT_OPEN_SAMPLE_ON_LAUNCH=1; final launch screenshot shows empty workspace with no prompt.
The empty workspace headline inherited white foreground on a cream canvas and was nearly invisible.
Fixed headline foregroundStyle to GraftTheme.ink; final screenshot shows readable headline.
SwiftPM parallel build race affected verification
Parallel Swift builds repeatedly failed with 'input file was modified during the build' on different files.
Run script now defaults to SWIFT_BUILD_JOBS=1; final --verify run passed.
